proposals.title: Second look: re-answer your misses blind before the answers unlock
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES: after a test they re-work the questions they got wrong or were unsure of, untimed and without seeing the answers, before anything is revealed. The report then says whether each miss was a knowledge gap or a slip.

WHEN AND WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE:
- Applies to mock, module and diagnostic, and to drills run with feedback at the end. Practice with instant feedback has already shown its keys, so it is excluded.
- On the first visit the hero shows the band, the delta and the route line as specced. Beside them sit a primary "Second look · 17 questions · untimed · about 15 min" and a quiet "Skip · show answers now".
- While a second look is pending, the grid, player and mistakes show only neutral cells and hide every key. For the owner, deps.access returns 'kept' for the sitting's keys.

WHICH QUESTIONS ARE IN THE SET:
- every Incorrect and Unanswered question;
- every flagged question;
- every conf 'unsure' or 'guess' question;
- right answers made in under 0:30;
- random right answers, topped up to 20% of the set (at least 2), so a question being in the set does not give away that it was wrong.

HOW IT RUNS:
- The set is served in sitting order in UI.workspace exam mode: calculator and reference on, no clock, per-question time recorded.
- The original pick is hidden, behind a "Show what I picked" toggle that is off by default.

WHAT IT SHOWS AFTER:
- One result line: "9 of 13 misses fixed on second look (execution) · 4 still wrong (concept) · 1 right answer changed (shaky)".
- A second band on the gauge, drawn as a hollow outline: "With time and care: 580–720 · the 60-point gap is execution, not knowledge".
- The keys then unlock, and the player opens at the first still-wrong question.
- Grid cells gain a cause corner: C concept, E execution, ~ shaky.

HOW IT FILES:
- Second-look answers file as repeat=1 (R8), so mastery stays honest.
- A still-wrong answer on a named misconception adds a hit and marks the trap 'confirmed'.
- A fixed answer marks it 'execution'. Review's kind filter and Fix read this.
- Skipping records state 'skipped'. The report then works as specced, and causes fall back to rules (see the Points ledger).
- A prefs key second_look (default on) can turn the step off.

WHY THE SCORE MOVES:
- Trying again before seeing the answer (pretesting and generation) makes the correction stick.
- It sorts every miss by its real cause without asking the student to judge themselves.
- It answers the most important study decision: learn content, or train pacing and care. Those need completely different practice.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Hide answers only hides the key box. You cannot re-answer, nothing is recorded, and nothing tells a slip from a concept gap. Their review shows the key at once, so the chance to try again cold is gone.

proposals.title: Points ledger: where the points went, and the cheapest ones to win back
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES: studies the misses worth the most points per minute first, not whatever feels hard. They see exactly which questions separate them from their target.

HOW EACH MISS IS VALUED: flip it to correct and re-run scoring.section_score on the same route. The value is computed on the unrounded centre (_interpolate) so single questions don't round to 0; totals are rounded to 10. For Module 1 misses the report also tests the 60% cut. When flipping would cross it, the row says "1 more right in M1 would have earned the harder Module 2 (ceiling 580 → 800)" and names the cheapest M1 misses that would have done it.

HOW EACH MISS GETS ONE CAUSE, first match wins:
1. Changed: right → wrong in the trail.
2. Time: a blank, or a wrong answer in the last 90 s of a module made in under 0:30.
3. Execution: fixed on the Second look, the filler 'near-miss arithmetic slip', or a rushed wrong answer under 0:30.
4. Guess: conf 'guess'.
5. Concept: everything else with a named misconception, or a grid-in miss.

WHAT IT SHOWS (region #ledger, placed right after the hero):
- One stacked bar: "140 points left on the table · Concept 60 · Execution 45 · Time 25 · Changed 10". Each segment is a review filter.
- A "Win back first" table, one row per skill or misconception. Columns:
  - points available;
  - estimated minutes to fix;
  - points per 10 min.
- How the minutes are estimated: the median number of clean questions learners needed to close traps on that template, times its median time. Fallback: 3 questions × 1:35, doubled for concept misses.
- "Most students at your level get this" tag: shown when the first-try rate on that (template, tier), among learners whose band overlaps yours, is 75% or more with n ≥ 20. Those rows sort to the top.
- A "Path to target" line: "4 questions from 700 on this section". It picks the fewest misses, greedily by value per cost, and lists them as chips (M2 Q4 easy · slip, M1 Q7 …) that open the player.
- The top 3 rows replace the generic coach pick in Up next: "Start: Circles · +30 · ~12 min".

WHY THE SCORE MOVES:
- Study time is the binding constraint. Ranking by points per minute stops students grinding hard questions while easy and medium points leak.
- A countable "4 questions from 700" goal is far more actionable and motivating than a band and a domain word.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's domain cards give a % and a 7-segment bar with mislabelled copy. The API returns a per-domain domainScore their UI never shows. Nothing links a single miss to points, and nothing ranks what to fix. The v2 spec's what-if only flips easy misses, all at once.

proposals.title: Recovery plan: every test schedules its own spaced, interleaved follow-up and proves the points came back
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES: the follow-up to a test becomes four steps spread over a week, and they can watch its points come back. It replaces one blocked "Fix these" run.

WHERE IT SHOWS:
- The report header's primary becomes a split "Start recovery · 4 steps". Its menu keeps every Fix variant from the spec.
- A step strip sits under the header: done steps ✓, the current step orange, future steps dated.

THE FOUR STEPS:
1. **Today: Second look** (proposal 1).
2. **Today or tomorrow: Repair set.**
   - Concept misses go through the worked-example ladder (proposal 5).
   - Execution misses become timed twins at 1:35 each.
   - Time misses become a 6-question timed run at the pace they missed.
   - Everything is interleaved across skills, never grouped by skill.
3. **Day +3: Check-in.**
   - One fresh twin per miss type.
   - About 30% of the items are templates the student got right, so lucky rights get checked too.
   - No hints. This is the same trap check-in as R9's 3-day step, so there is no double schedule.
4. **Day +7: Mini retest.**
   - 10–15 questions under test rules: the missed and unsure templates on fresh seeds.
   - It ends in a verdict: "Recovered 11 of 13 miss types · +70 of 140 points (est.)".

THE RECOVERED METER:
- The hero shows "+70 of 140 recovered".
- It sums the ledger values of misses whose trap closed cleanly and passed its check-in, and updates live whenever the student reopens the report.

OTHER SCREENS:
- The steps appear as Plan tasks and in Today's up-next chain.
- Results sitting cards show "Recovery 2/4 · check-in Sep 26".
- If the student ignores it, the steps slide once. After 14 days they fold into Review's normal redo list.

WHY THE SCORE MOVES:
- Spacing and interleaving are the most robust findings for durable math skill.
- "Fix all 13 now" feels like mastery, but the fix fades before test day.
- The day +7 retest gives the proof that keeps a student practising.

proposals.title: Worked-example ladder in the player for concept misses
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES: on a concept miss, instead of jumping straight to a fresh twin at full difficulty, they climb a short ladder. It sits in the same inline tile, and the spec's twin becomes rung 3.

THE RUNGS:
1. **See one solved.**
   - A fresh seed of the same template, rendered solved: the stem, the key marked, the seed's own rationale.
   - The option that the student's misconception produces with these new numbers is tagged: "Your mistake gives 184 here".
   - This works because every seed has its own reasons[] and rationale.
   - Nothing is filed.
2. **Your turn, with a hint.**
   - A second fresh seed.
   - A "Hint" button reveals the template's optional hint field. The fallback is the first clause of that seed's rationale, then "Watch for: <your misconception>".
   - A right answer after a hint files as guess=1: half credit, and it does not close the trap (R8).
3. **On your own**: the specced twin, which can close the trap.
4. **Spot the trap** (Review's), optional.

- Progress dots in the tile.
- The rung reached is stored per miss.
- The Mistakes list shows "Rung 2 of 3".
- Execution misses skip straight to rung 3, timed.

- The worked-example effect: studying a solved example and then solving a similar one teaches novices more than solving alone.
- Fading support then builds independence.
- Seeing your own mistake produce a specific wrong option on new numbers trains you to recognise the trap.

proposals.title: Confidence calibration and the 'sure but wrong' list
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES:
- Sees which misconceptions they actually hold (they were sure, and wrong) and fixes those first.
- Learns whether to trust their gut on test day.

IT FILLS A HOLE:
- Tests (§3.4.7) says the report must render confidence calibration, but §3.5 specifies no region for it.
- Tests' Sure / Unsure / Guess tags are off by default; when they are off, flags stand in.

THE REGION (#calib):
- A 3×2 table: rows Sure / Unsure / Guess, columns Right / Wrong.
- Each row gives a count and %, e.g. "Sure 26 · 23 right (88%)".
- A verdict line, for example:
  - "Your sure answers are trustworthy. Unsure ones were right 64% of the time, so answer and move on rather than sinking time."
  - "You were sure of 3 wrong answers: these are beliefs, not slips."
- Guesses are compared with chance: "right 31%, chance 25%".

IN MISTAKES AND RECOVERY:
- A new first group, "Sure and wrong · 3", sits above Open.
- Those misconceptions enter the recovery plan at rung 1, and get an extra check-in at day 10.

WHEN TAGS ARE OFF:
- Flagged counts as unsure.
- A one-tap "Turn on confidence tags for your next test" writes the prefs key, with the helper "One tap per question. Shows which mistakes you're sure of."

ON RESULTS:
- A calibration trend across sittings: sure accuracy 88% → 93%.
- The unsure rate per skill. A skill where most answers are unsure is not yet fluent, even when they are right.

WHY THE SCORE MOVES:
- The hypercorrection effect: errors made with high confidence, once corrected with feedback, are the ones corrected most durably, but only if they are surfaced.
- Well-calibrated students spend test time on unsure questions instead of re-checking sure ones.

proposals.title: Clock replay, skip-and-return what-if, and a fluency map
proposals.what:
WHAT THE STUDENT DOES: trains pacing as a skill. They see where they fell behind, and they practise their slow skills at the right speed.

ON THE REPORT, a clock replay per module in #pace:
- A step line of question reached against elapsed module time (0–35:00), over the ideal 95 s/question diagonal.
- Visits back to flagged questions are drawn as return loops.
- Markers: "Behind from Q12 · 4:10 behind at Q18".
- A "Starved" callout when long wrong solves came just before rushed or blank ones: "M2 Q19 took 4:12 and was wrong; Q20–22 got 0:40 between them".
- A skip-and-return what-if: "Leaving Q19 at 2:00 frees 2:12 for Q20–22 (easy): est. +20 points". It uses the ledger values, with a flat 60% success assumed on the freed questions, and is labelled "est.".
- A blank policy line: "2 blanks: a guess on each is worth ~+5 points on average; never leave one".

ON RESULTS, a fluency map (#fluency): a 2×2 of the 19 skills.
- Accuracy (y, split at 70%) against relative pace (x): the median of ms divided by the expected time for the difficulty (easy 60 s, medium 95 s, hard 130 s), over the last 40 answers.
- Each quadrant has a named drill with the right timing:
  - Slow and right → "Fluency drill" at timing custom:80.
  - Fast and wrong → "Slow down": untimed, with the rule card "re-read what it asks".
  - Slow and wrong → "Learn it": the worked-example ladder.
  - Fast and right → "Keep warm".

WHY THE SCORE MOVES:
- Easy and medium blanks at the end of a module are the most common avoidable loss on the digital SAT, and pacing can be trained.
- A slow skill that is accurate needs speed work. A fast skill that is inaccurate needs slowing down. One generic drill fixes neither.

proposals.title: Error families: the habits behind your misconceptions, across skills
proposals.what:
THE PROBLEM: the bank has about 882 distinct normalised misconception labels over 386 templates, measured by sampling one seed per template. Review merges only identical norms (79 recur). Habits hide across skills.

THE FAMILY LAYER: a one-off mapping file, satbank/families.json {norm → family}, built by keyword rules plus a manual pass. test_flow asserts that every reason in the catalogue maps. About 12 families:
- Sign or direction
- Wrong operation (added vs subtracted, multiplied vs divided)
- Stopped a step early (answered an intermediate value)
- Answered a different quantity than asked
- Formula part swapped (radius/diameter, area/perimeter)
- Percent and decimal
- Order swapped (coordinates, ratio, x/y)
- Misread a graph or table
- Units and rates
- Counting solutions or cases
- Statistics interpretation
- Arithmetic slip

ON THE REPORT: a "Habits" strip under Mistakes: "3 of your 11 misconceptions are 'Stopped a step early', in 3 skills". Each family chip filters the review.

ON RESULTS (#habits):
- Family counts over the last 5 sittings, with a trend.
- A "Habit drill" per family: fresh items across templates whose distractors belong to that family (the drill 'want' field matched by family).
- The family's checking routine shown as a rule card before each item, e.g. "Before you choose: re-read the last line and underline what is asked."

WHY THE SCORE MOVES:
- Habits carry across topics. Fixing "stopped a step early" once pays off in every skill, and per-template repair can't reach that.
- Naming the habit lets the student install one checking routine instead of 20 separate fixes.

proposals.title: Where your points went: a points ledger on every scored sitting
proposals.what:
Server: /api/session/{sid}/results gains a `ledger` for mock, module and diagnostic sittings, built by a pure function scoring.ledger(questions, answers, route) that sits next to section_score. It returns three things:
- per_q[qid].pts: the midpoint gain if that one miss alone had been right. It re-runs score() and section_score() on the same route and rounds to 5.
- buckets: misses flipped cumulatively, easy, then medium, then hard, then blanks, with each bucket's gain, plus route_cap (uncapped high minus 580, when capped). By construction the buckets and route_cap add up exactly to the all-right midpoint minus your midpoint.
- route_savers: when Module 1 is at most 2 right short of ceil(0.6 x asked), the M1 misses ranked easiest first.

Report:
- Under the gauge, a horizontal waterfall bar: "All right on this route 710-790 -> easy misses -35 -> medium -50 -> hard -40 -> blanks -15 -> you 520-660". Each segment is a button that filters the review to that bucket.
- A route line: "Module 1: 13/22 (59%). One more right would have sent you to the harder Module 2 and lifted the 580 cap (up to +80)." Route-saver cells get a small up-arrow marker.
- Every mistake row, table row and player header shows "about -15 pts". The table gets a sortable Points column, and Mistakes sorting gains "Most points" (the default for tests).
- Domain cards show "-60 pts" and sort by it.
- The primary Fix pill becomes "Win back about 60 pts · 9 questions · 14 min". It orders misses by points per expected minute (pts / max(avg_ms, 60 s)) and caps the set at prefs.minutes. The existing ⌄ variants stay, plus "Everything · 13".

Results overview: a "Gap to target, decomposed" card beside the estimate. It averages the last 3 scored sittings' ledgers by bucket and by domain, e.g. "Target 700 · 40 above your estimate. Easy slips 20 · Advanced Math hard 25 · blanks 10", with a Start button per row that drills those sittings' misses in that bucket.

"How this is estimated" says it is our easy 1 / medium 2 / hard 3 weighting.
proposals.beats: Their report gives "Total Score 420/1600 · 4 of 49 correct". Their plan's "Score gap" tile is a bare "1000 now, 1400 target". Their API returns a per-domain domainScore that no screen shows. Nothing tells a student which questions cost what. The v2 spec's what-if line covers one tier only. This prices every miss, explains the routing cap in points, and turns Fix into the highest-payoff 14 minutes in one tap. On theirs, finding the cheapest points is impossible.
proposals.needs: F4: scoring.py ledger() with an assert check in server/checks/s6.py (the buckets sum to ceiling minus midpoint, every pts >= 0). S6: api_results field. F4: estimate.py for the gap card. R11: prefs.minutes. F5: the drill body (§2.6) must accept an ordered `only` list and keep its order.

proposals.title: Second look: re-answer every miss before the key shows, and separate slips from gaps
proposals.what:
Opening a miss:
- The first time an Incorrect or Unanswered question opens in the player (from Review mistakes, a cell, a mistake row or a chip), it opens in Second look.
- The key mark, your old pick, the answer boxes, the reasons and the explanation are hidden. A header chip reads "Second look · no clock".
- A–D / 1–4 pick and Enter checks. A grid-in uses the normal field.

Checking:
- Check files an attempt through R21's review mode with repeat=1 (left out of mastery, R8) and source 'second-look', then reveals everything.
- The verdict line reads "Right on a second look: a slip", or "Wrong again · same trap: <label>", or "Wrong again · a different trap: <label>".
- A quiet "Just show me" (key V) reveals without filing.

Storage and counts:
- Each look is stored per (learner, session, qid) as {at, second: right|wrong|skipped, reason}.
- The report gets a tile "Second look · 5 slips · 6 gaps · 2 to go" and Show filters Slips / Gaps. Mistake rows get a Slip or Gap chip.
- A gap sets the trap kind to misconception; a slip sets R9's 'slip' kind.

Actions:
- Fix ⌄ gains "Gaps only · 6" (a teaching set) and "Slips, timed · 5" (paced at 1:35, to train care under time).
- The player shows "Looked at 7 of 13".
- Hide answers (H) stays for correct questions.
proposals.beats: Their Hide answers hides the key, but you still cannot re-answer. So a student never learns whether a miss was not knowing or rushing. The v2 spec's hidden pick files nothing, and it contradicts R21, where a re-answer files a repeat. Ours turns every review step into retrieval practice plus a diagnosis. Thirteen misses take about 26 keystrokes: a letter and Enter each.

proposals.what:
New section order:
- header

- Takeaways
- Mistakes
- Question review
- tiles · modules · domains · skills · difficulty & format · pace · changes · how you answered

Takeaways: three cards from a server `debrief[]`, rule-based and ranked by points at stake. Examples:
- "Biggest leak: Linear inequalities · 3 misses · about 40 pts · the same trap twice" [Fix 3]
- "Pace: 3 rushed misses in Module 2's last 6 minutes · about 20 pts" [Paced set]
- "Win: Geometry 7/7, up from 4/7 on Section #6"
Other rules: near the route cut, 2 or more right-to-wrong changes, 2 or more sure-but-wrong, surprise misses. Each card has one primary action and a quiet "Put in tomorrow's plan".

Jump bar: sticky under the page bar once the hero scrolls away. It reads "Score · Mistakes 13 · Questions 44 · Time · Skills · Changes 5", and scroll-spy marks the current section.

The only way into a question is to scroll to the grid and click a square, and there is no misses-only filter (All / R&W / Math / Flagged). The v2 spec puts Mistakes 10th of 12 sections, below pace and answer changes, which is thousands of pixels down at 390px. proposals.title: An error log that fills itself: a cause on every miss, one tap to correct, trended over time
proposals.what:
Each miss gets a pre-filled cause from evidence. The first match wins:
1. Ran out of time: a blank in a module whose clock hit 0.
2. Changed away from right: the trail holds the key before the final answer.
3. Crossed out the key: qstate.struck includes it.
4. Rushed: under 30 s.
5. Slip: right on the second look.
6. Grid-in entry: grid_equal fails but the value is the key before rounding or within 1% of it (0.66 for 2/3).
7. Guess: conf = Guess.
8. Misconception: a named distractor, and the second look was wrong.
9. Didn't know: everything else.

Player:
- A chip under the status chip reads "Cause: Rushed (auto) ▾".
- One tap offers Careless · Misread · Didn't know · Ran out of time · Calculator · Other. Keys: C, then 1–6.
- "auto" drops once confirmed.

Report: a "Why you missed" stacked bar (13 misses by cause, with P1 points). Each segment is a filter.

Results: "Why you miss, over time", one 100% stacked bar per scored sitting (last 10), with a line such as "Careless misses fell from 45% to 20% since Sep 13".

Fix by cause:
- Careless or Rushed -> a paced set
- Didn't know -> that skill's practice
- Grid-in entry -> the grid-in rules card plus 5 grid-ins
- Ran out of time -> a pacing drill of the module's last-third question types

The CSV includes the cause.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep records no cause, and its review payload has no time, skill or difficulty to infer one from. Tutors make students keep this log by hand in a spreadsheet. Ours is prefilled from the answer trail, time, eliminations, confidence and the second look, and correcting it costs one tap.
proposals.needs: S5: qstate trail, struck, conf and ms, plus the module clock end. Proposal 2's looks. F4: a cause column on the looks table. scoring.grid_equal plus a near-value check. S6: the /api/stats aggregate.

Player:

Elsewhere:

- The difficulty and format rows show "You 2:24 · students who got them right 1:50".

proposals.title: Clock replay: where each module's 35 minutes went
proposals.what:
Per module, a horizontal timeline from 0:00 to 35:00:
- One lane of blocks in visit order: width is time and fill is final status. Revisits sit in a second lane.
- Markers: flag set, answer change (↺), a dashed pace curve (where 1:35 a question would have put you, shaded ahead or behind), and the clock end.

Auto summary lines:
- "4:30 behind pace by Q15, with 2:10 for the last 7"

On a phone the lane runs vertically. The per-question pace bars stay as the sorted view.

proposals.title: Instant key re-check inside Report a problem
proposals.what:
When the category is "Wrong answer key", "Two answers are right" or "No right answer", the dialog calls GET /api/report/check?session=&qid= before Send.

Server: it regenerates (template, seed) and runs satbank.audit.audit(item), the template's independent solver. For a grid-in it also runs grid_equal on the student's entry.

What the dialog shows:
- Solver agrees: "Re-checked just now by an independent solver: D (73 ≤ t ≤ 111)", plus the rationale's key line.
- Grid-in entry refused: "Your 0.66 isn't accepted. The grid fits 4 characters, so 2/3 goes in as .6666 or .6667."
- Solver fails: "Our solver disagrees with this key. It's pulled while we check." The (template, seed) goes on a hold list that deps.access (R19) consults, so nobody else is served it.

Send stays available ("Still think it's wrong? A person reads every report"), and the stored report carries the check result for the admin.

Every template here ships an independent solver (audit.py per topic), so most key disputes are answered in a second, and a genuinely bad key is pulled for everyone at once.

proposals.title: Where your points went: points per miss by cause, a route-cliff line and a live what-if
proposals.what: SERVER: results gains `points`. For each miss i, gain_i = the section midpoint with only i flipped to the key, minus the actual midpoint. It re-runs scoring.score + section_score on the same route: 44 pure calls, a few ms. For a lower route it adds route_gap {m1_right, needed: 14 of 22 (ROUTE_UP_AT 0.6), short_by, cap: 580}, and gains past the cap read 0 with capped:true. Each miss gets one cause, the first rule that matches, derived when the report is read and never stored: TIME (blank, not reached, or answered in the module's last 10% of the clock in under 30 s); SLIP (right on Second look (proposal 3); before a second look, 'likely slip' = easy or medium, under 45 s, and a measured level of 3 or lower when one exists); TRAP (the pick names a misconception); GAP (the rest: an unnamed grid-in miss, or still wrong on second look). New POST /api/session/{sid}/whatif {flip:[qid]} returns {estimate, capped}. Module 2 is never re-routed, and the reply says so. HERO: under the gauge, one stacked bar 'Lost about 180 points' in four labelled segments, e.g. Time 40 (3) · Slips 55 (5) · Traps 65 (4) · Gaps 20 (1). Clicking a segment sets the review filter cause=<x> and scrolls to it. Helper: 'Points on the band's midpoint, using this report's own scoring (easy 1, medium 2, hard 3).' Route-cliff line, when route=lower and short_by ≤ 3: '1 more right in Module 1 would have earned the harder Module 2 and lifted the 580 cap. Your easiest Module 1 misses: M1 Q3 · M1 Q9', each chip opening the player. EVERYWHERE: every miss shows its gain ('≈ +19 pts') in the grid tooltip, the mistakes row, a 'Worth' table column (sortable) and the player header. WHAT-IF MODE: a toolbar toggle 'What if…'. While it is on, clicking a miss cell marks it with a ghost ✓, and the gauge redraws after a 150 ms debounce. Presets: 'Flip my slips' · 'Flip easy misses' · 'Flip time losses' · Reset. The spec's single whatif sentence becomes the 'Flip easy misses' preset.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep shows one score, counts, and a domainScore their UI never prints. Nothing says what each miss cost or why it was lost, and they cannot: their payload has no time, no skill and no misconception per option. Adaptive routing, the most misunderstood part of the digital SAT, is never explained. Ours turns a report into a price list of recoverable points.
proposals.needs: scoring.py stays pure and reusable (F4). Per-question ms from qstate (R7, S5 runner) for the TIME cause. Proposal 3 for confirmed slips. drill.levels() measured level (Practice §levels) is optional. UI.gauge redraw hook (F1 charts.js). A cause filter in the review filter bar.

RESULTS gains recovery {recovered:[qid], slipping:[qid], open:[qid], points_recovered, points_open, now_estimate}. now_estimate re-runs scoring with the recovered misses flipped. Prove it starts Tests' custom test {source:'misses', from_session:sid}: fresh seeds of each missed template, 95 s each, no feedback until hand-in, cfg.parent=sid. When it finishes, its report links back ('Proven 9 of 13 → Section #7 rescored'), and the proven cells take the Fixed-since token (§2.3), now driven by proof and not only by a trap closing. proposals.title: Instant key checker on reports, and automatic rescoring when a question is fixed

Attempts and traps are corrected. Affected reports show a strip: 'M1 Q7 was corrected on Oct 2 after a report. This sitting was rescored: 520–660 → 530–670.' The reporter sees 'Your report fixed this question type for every future student' in Settings › Your reports. Old grid-in misses are renamed the same way when a template gains spr_mistakes.
